newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kinshasa summit ends, plans mission to EU on aid. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Kinshasa summit ends, plans mission to EU on aid. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]

text.p: Democratic Congo's President Laurent Kabila and the leaders of Uganda and Rwanda agreed on Wednesday to send envoys to the European Union to seek aid for a key regional road project, a communique said.

Kabila said he and Ugandan leader Yoweri Museveni and Rwandan President Pasteur Bizimungu (corrects from Pascal Bizimungu) agreed on the urgent reconstruction of the 500-km (300-mile) Goma-Kisangani road.
"It was decided to send a common delegation this month to revive a loan which was approved (by the EU) for the reconstruction of this road," Kabila told reporters.
An EU mission announced last week that Brussels was ready to resume cooperation with the ex-Zaire after a five-year freeze amid charges of misrule by ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko.
There were no details of the EU loan or the estimated cost of the road project at today's valuation.
"It is a principal route which is going to serve the three countries," Kabila said, expanding on a joint communique.
Kabila toppled Mobutu in May after a seven-month guerrilla campaign launched from the vast country's eastern provinces.
The road from Goma on Lake Kivu to Kisangani, the third largest town in the renamed Democratic Republic of the Congo, gave Kabila's guerrillas vital access to the interior.
Kabila has targeted reopening the country, which is the size of western Europe, as a priority objective leading to a relaunch of a potentially rich economy but which was neglected by Mobutu.
The former rebel chief and the two other leaders, who backed Kabila's armed campaign, began talks on Tuesday as part of new Congo's policy of reinforcing links with its neighbours.
Kabila and Museveni agreed in separate talks on Tuesday to embark on a joint search for oil around Lake Albert and Lake Edward which stradle their territories.
The summit also agreed to seek the intervention of Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe, the chairman of the Organisation of African Unity, in the ethnic and political conflict in Congo-Brazzaville.
Fighting between troops loyal to President Pascal Lisouba and the militia of ex-military ruler Denis Sassou Nguesso since June has paralysed Brazzaville, across the river from Kinshasa.
Mediation by a United Nations envoy and Gabon's President Omar Bongo has so far failed to yield a breakthrough.
"We discussed this problem. It is worrying," Kabila said.
Kinshasa hosted a larger regional summit in July and Museveni and Bizimungu have paid three previous official visits to the city since Kabila took power.

In a flurry of diplomatic activity, retired Tanzanian president Julius Nyerere also arrived in Kinshasa on Tuesday for talks with Kabila. Officials said the president of Eritrea, Issaias Afewerki, was arriving later on Wednesday.
